query: Which adaptive experimental designs (sequential allocation, group-sequential, or bandit-style interventions) can reduce required interventions while preserving causal identifiability?

response.query: Which adaptive experimental designs (sequential allocation, group-sequential, or bandit-style interventions) can reduce required interventions while preserving causal identifiability?
response.answer: Group-sequential and bandit-style interventions can reduce required interventions while preserving causal identifiability. These designs allow for interim analyses and adaptive modifications based on accumulating data.
